statute_title: Driving Under the Influence of Alcohol, Other Drug or Drugs, Intoxicating Compound or Compounds or Any Combination Thereof
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (1st/2nd offense); Class 4 Felony (3rd offense)
elements: Operated a motor vehicle
On a public highway or other public or private property used for vehicular travel
While under the influence of alcohol (BAC 0.08+) or other drugs or combination that rendered the person incapable of safely driving
mandatory_minimum: 100 hours community service or 5 days imprisonment for second offense
enhancements: Aggravated DUI (Class 4 Felony): 3rd+ offense, DUI without valid license, DUI in school zone
Class 2 Felony: DUI causing great bodily harm
Class 1 Felony: DUI causing death
BAC 0.16+ doubles minimum fine on first offense
Presence of child under 16 in vehicle: additional Class 6 Felony charge
notes: Illinois DUI law includes 11 separate bases for DUI under 625 ILCS 5/11-501(a). Statutory summary suspension of driving privileges applies automatically on arrest.

statute_title: Driving Under the Influence — First Offense
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: First DUI conviction or supervision
Operated a motor vehicle while impaired by alcohol or drugs
enhancements: If BAC 0.16+: mandatory minimum $500 fine and 100 hours community service
If transporting child under 16: additional Class 6 Felony (720 ILCS 5/12-3.05)
notes: First offense DUI is eligible for court supervision, which avoids a conviction on record if successfully completed. Minimum 1-year statutory summary suspension.

statute_title: Driving Under the Influence — Repeat Offense
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (2nd); Class 4 to Class 2 Felony (3rd+)
penalty_min: 5 days imprisonment or 240 hours community service (2nd offense)
elements: Prior DUI conviction or supervision on record
Current DUI offense proven under 625 ILCS 5/11-501
mandatory_minimum: 5 days or 240 community service hours for 2nd offense
enhancements: 3rd offense: Class 4 Felony (3-year revocation)
4th offense: Class 4 Felony (lifetime revocation)
5th offense: Class 1 Felony
6th+ offense: Class X Felony
notes: Illinois maintains a lifetime look-back for prior DUI offenses. 3rd+ offense results in permanent felony record.

statute_title: Driving Under the Influence of Drugs or Intoxicating Compound
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (1st); Class 4 Felony (3rd+)
elements: Operated a motor vehicle
While under the influence of any drug or combination of drugs that rendered driver incapable of safely driving
OR with presence of cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine, or cannabis metabolite exceeding statutory thresholds
enhancements: Same felony escalation as alcohol DUI for repeat offenses
Cannabis DUI threshold: 5 nanograms THC per mL blood or 10 ng per mL other bodily substance
notes: Per se drug DUI under 11-501(a)(6) applies to cannabis. Zero-tolerance for other controlled substances under 11-501(a)(5).

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Class 4 Felony if great bodily harm results
elements: Operated a vehicle on any highway or private property used for vehicle traffic
With willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property
OR used an incline in a highway to cause the vehicle to become airborne
enhancements: Class 4 Felony if reckless driving causes great bodily harm, permanent disability, or disfigurement
Aggravated if committed in a school zone

statute_title: Motor Vehicle Accident Involving Death or Personal Injuries — Duty to Stop
offense_class: Class 4 Felony (injury); Class 1 Felony (death)
elements: Driver of a vehicle involved in an accident resulting in injury or death
Failed to immediately stop at the scene
Failed to provide name, address, and vehicle registration information
Failed to render reasonable assistance to injured persons
enhancements: Class 1 Felony if accident caused death
Immediate revocation of driving privileges
notes: Property-damage-only hit and run is a separate offense under 625 ILCS 5/11-402 (Class A Misdemeanor).

offense_class: Class 3 Felony; Class 2 Felony (aggravated)
elements: Operated a motor vehicle in a reckless manner
Unintentional killing of another person resulted
Acts constituted conscious disregard of a substantial and unjustifiable risk
enhancements: Class 2 Felony (aggravated): two or more deaths result
DUI-related death charged separately under 625 ILCS 5/11-501(d) as aggravated DUI Class X
School zone or construction zone: enhanced penalties
notes: DUI-related vehicular death is typically charged as aggravated DUI causing death under 625 ILCS 5/11-501(d) rather than reckless homicide, though both may be charged.

offense_class: Class 3 Felony
elements: Operated a motor vehicle in a reckless manner
Caused the unintentional death of another person
enhancements: Aggravated: Class 2 Felony for death in school zone or construction zone
notes: Illinois does not separately title vehicular manslaughter — the offense falls under the reckless homicide statute.

statute_title: Driving While Driver's License, Permit, or Privilege to Operate a Motor Vehicle is Suspended or Revoked
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; up to Class 4 Felony (3rd+ offense or revoked for DUI)
elements: Operated a motor vehicle
While driver's license, permit, or privilege to operate was suspended or revoked
mandatory_minimum: 10 days imprisonment or 30 days community service for 2nd violation during DUI suspension
enhancements: Class 4 Felony: 4th+ offense or when suspension/revocation is for DUI conviction
Class 2 Felony: 4th conviction when revocation was for reckless homicide or aggravated DUI

statute_title: Fleeing or Attempting to Elude a Police Officer
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Class 4 Felony (aggravated)
elements: Driver of a vehicle on a highway
Willfully failed or refused to obey a direction to stop by a police officer driving an authorized emergency vehicle with siren or lights engaged
enhancements: Aggravated (Class 4 Felony): reckless driving during flight, exceeding speed limit by 21+ mph, disobeying 2+ traffic control devices
Class 3 Felony if aggravated AND caused bodily harm or accident

statute_title: Possession of Alcoholic Beverage in Motor Vehicle
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Transported or possessed an alcoholic beverage in a motor vehicle
While operating the vehicle on a highway
Container had a broken seal, partially removed contents, or was open
notes: Passengers may be charged as well. Exceptions exist for passengers in buses, taxis, and limousines.

statute_title: Implied Consent — Refusal of Chemical Testing
offense_class: Civil/Administrative (not a separate criminal charge)
elements: Arrested for DUI
Refused to submit to or failed to complete chemical testing (breath, blood, or urine)
enhancements: First refusal: 12-month statutory summary suspension
Second+ refusal: 36-month suspension
Refusal may be used as evidence at DUI trial
notes: Refusal is an administrative violation triggering statutory summary suspension, not a separate criminal charge in Illinois.

offense_class: Class 4 Felony (small amounts); up to Class X Felony (large amounts)
elements: Knowingly possessed a controlled substance
Substance was listed in Schedules I through V of the Illinois Controlled Substances Act
Without a valid prescription or other lawful authority
mandatory_minimum: 6 years for 100 to 400g Class X amounts
enhancements: Class 1 Felony: heroin, cocaine, or opioids 15+ grams
Class X Felony: heroin or cocaine 100+ grams (mandatory 6 to 30 years)
Enhanced if possession within 1,000 feet of school
notes: Illinois removed cannabis possession from this statute for amounts under 30g. See 720 ILCS 550/4 for cannabis.

offense_class: Civil infraction (under 30g); Class A Misdemeanor (30 to 100g); Class 4 Felony (100 to 500g)
penalty_max: Civil fine (under 10g); 1 year (30 to 100g); 3 years (100 to 500g)
elements: Possessed cannabis
Amount exceeded legal adult-use limits (30g flower for non-registered users)
enhancements: 500g to 2,000g: Class 3 Felony
2,000g to 5,000g: Class 2 Felony
5,000g+: Class 1 Felony
Enhanced penalties within 1,000 feet of school
notes: Illinois legalized recreational cannabis in 2020. Adults 21+ may possess up to 30g flower, 5g concentrate, 500mg THC in products.

offense_class: Class 4 Felony (under 15g); Class 1 Felony (15 to 100g); Class X Felony (100g+)
penalty_max: 1 to 3 years (Class 4); 4 to 15 years (Class 1); 6 to 30 years (Class X)
elements: Knowingly possessed cocaine or a substance containing cocaine
Amount falls within charged quantity bracket
enhancements: Class X with 6-year minimum: 100 to 400g
Class X with 9-year minimum: 400 to 900g
Class X with 12-year minimum: 900g+

offense_class: Class 3 Felony (under 5g); Class 2 Felony (5 to 15g); up to Class X Felony (100g+)
penalty_max: 2 to 5 years (Class 3); 3 to 7 years (Class 2); 6 to 30+ years (Class X)
elements: Knowingly possessed methamphetamine or a substance containing methamphetamine
mandatory_minimum: 6 years (100 to 400g meth); escalating mandatory minimums for larger amounts
enhancements: Class X for 100g+: mandatory 6 to 30 years
Enhanced if within 1,000 feet of school, daycare, or public park
notes: Illinois Methamphetamine Control and Community Protection Act (720 ILCS 646) governs meth offenses separately from the general Controlled Substances Act.

statute_title: Possession of Heroin or Opioid Controlled Substances
offense_class: Class 4 Felony (under 15g); Class 1 Felony (15 to 100g); Class X Felony (100g+)
penalty_max: 1 to 3 years (Class 4); 4 to 15 years (Class 1); 6 to 30 years (Class X)
elements: Knowingly possessed heroin, fentanyl, or a Schedule I or II opioid controlled substance
Without a valid prescription
mandatory_minimum: 6 years (100 to 400g heroin); 9 years (400 to 900g); 12 years (900g+)
enhancements: Fentanyl: Class X triggered at lower thresholds due to mixture weight calculations under 720 ILCS 570/402(c)

statute_title: Possession of Prescription Controlled Substance Without Valid Prescription
offense_class: Class 4 Felony
elements: Knowingly possessed a Schedule II through V prescription controlled substance
Without a valid prescription issued in the defendant's name
enhancements: Higher felony class based on weight — same Schedule II drug thresholds apply

statute_title: Manufacture or Delivery of Controlled Substances
offense_class: Class 1 Felony (small amounts); Class X Felony (large amounts)
penalty_max: 4 to 15 years (Class 1); 6 to 30 years to natural life (Class X)
fine_max: $250,000 or street value, whichever is greater
elements: Knowingly delivered a controlled substance to another person
OR possessed with intent to deliver
Substance was a Schedule I or II controlled substance
enhancements: Class X with extended term: delivery within 1,000 feet of school or public park
Enhanced if delivery to person under 18
Continuing narcotics conspiracy under 720 ILCS 570/405.2
notes: 720 ILCS 570/401 lists specific substance thresholds with escalating felony classes.

offense_class: Class 2 Felony (small delivery); Class X Felony (large amounts)
elements: Knowingly delivered a controlled substance to another person
Without legal authority to distribute
enhancements: Near school zone: enhanced classification
To person under 18: Class X regardless of quantity
notes: Same statute as drug trafficking; distinction based on quantity thresholds in 720 ILCS 570/401 subsections.

offense_class: Class 1 to Class X Felony depending on substance
elements: Manufactured, produced, prepared, or processed a controlled substance
OR possessed chemicals and equipment with intent to manufacture
enhancements: Meth manufacturing: Class X offense under 720 ILCS 646/15 (6 to 30 years)
Manufacturing within 1,000 feet of school: Class X mandatory
notes: Meth manufacturing is governed by the Methamphetamine Control and Community Protection Act (720 ILCS 646). All other manufacturing falls under the Controlled Substances Act.

offense_class: Civil violation (first offense); Class A Misdemeanor (subsequent)
elements: Possessed drug paraphernalia with intent to use for introducing a controlled substance into the body
OR to pack, store, contain, or conceal a controlled substance
notes: Illinois revised paraphernalia law in 2016. First offense is civil infraction. Needle and syringe possession for personal use decriminalized under 720 ILCS 635.

statute_title: Fraudulent Acquisition of Prescription Controlled Substance
offense_class: Class 3 Felony
elements: Obtained or attempted to obtain a controlled substance by fraud, deceit, misrepresentation, or subterfuge
OR forged or altered a prescription
OR impersonated a licensed practitioner
enhancements: Class 2 Felony if value exceeds $500 or multiple prescriptions obtained
Professional license revocation for licensed practitioners

statute_title: Possession of Controlled Substance with Intent to Deliver
offense_class: Class 1 Felony (small amounts); Class X Felony (large amounts)
elements: Possessed a controlled substance
Intent to deliver inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, currency, or other circumstantial evidence
enhancements: Same enhancements as delivery charges under 720 ILCS 570/401
notes: Illinois treats possession with intent as equivalent to delivery under the same statute and sentencing schedule.

offense_class: Class M Felony (most serious felony in Illinois)
penalty_max: 60 years; natural life for aggravated circumstances
elements: Killed an individual without lawful justification
AND either: (1) intended to kill or do great bodily harm; (2) knew act would cause death; OR (3) was attempting or committing a forcible felony (felony murder)
mandatory_minimum: 20 years; 60 years for killing law enforcement or during predicate felony
enhancements: Natural life (no parole): multiple murders, murder for hire, torture, murder of officer or firefighter, murder during armed robbery, murder of witness
Death penalty abolished in Illinois (2011)
Truth-in-sentencing: must serve 100% of sentence
notes: Illinois abolished the death penalty in 2011. Natural life imprisonment is the maximum.

offense_class: Class 1 Felony
elements: Elements of first degree murder are present
AND at the time of killing defendant was acting under sudden and intense passion resulting from serious provocation
OR defendant believed circumstances justified the killing but that belief was unreasonable (imperfect self-defense)
enhancements: If victim was officer or firefighter: minimum sentence increases
Prior felony convictions increase sentencing range
notes: Second degree murder is an affirmative mitigating defense to first degree murder. Defendant must present evidence by preponderance of the evidence.

statute_title: Second Degree Murder (encompasses voluntary manslaughter concept)
offense_class: Class 1 Felony
elements: Intentional killing
Under sudden and intense passion resulting from serious provocation by the victim
notes: Illinois does not use the term 'voluntary manslaughter' — the concept is subsumed in Second Degree Murder under 720 ILCS 5/9-2.

offense_class: Class 3 Felony; Class 2 Felony (with deadly weapon)
elements: Unintentionally killed an individual
Acts were performed recklessly — conscious disregard of a substantial and unjustifiable risk of death
enhancements: Class 2 Felony if committed with a firearm or other deadly weapon

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor to Class 3 Felony depending on victim or weapon
elements: Committed an assault (placing a person in reasonable apprehension of receiving a battery)
AND used a deadly weapon, discharged a firearm from a vehicle, acted from disguise, targeted a protected-class victim, or acted in a public place
enhancements: Class 3 Felony: assault with firearm, against police, firefighter, EMT, teacher, or elderly person
Class 2 Felony: discharge of firearm or specific aggravating victim categories
Class 1 Felony: firearm discharge causing injury
notes: 720 ILCS 5/12-2 lists 15+ categories of aggravating factors.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor
elements: Engaged in conduct that placed another in reasonable apprehension of receiving a battery
Without lawful authority
notes: Illinois assault does not require physical contact. Battery (720 ILCS 5/12-3) is the completed physical contact offense.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Knowingly, without legal justification
Made physical contact of insulting or provoking nature with an individual
OR caused bodily harm to an individual
enhancements: Aggravated Battery (720 ILCS 5/12-3.05): Class 3 to Class X felony depending on aggravating factor

offense_class: Class 3 Felony to Class X Felony depending on circumstances
elements: Committed a battery
AND: caused great bodily harm, permanent disability, or disfigurement; used a deadly weapon; victim was a protected class; committed on a public way; used a caustic substance; OR discharged a firearm
enhancements: Class X Felony: battery with firearm causing great bodily harm
15-year mandatory add-on if personally discharged a firearm causing great bodily harm (720 ILCS 5/33A-2)
notes: 720 ILCS 5/12-3.05 contains 20+ categories. Firearm discharge add-ons are mandatory consecutive under 720 ILCS 5/33A-2.

offense_class: Class 2 Felony; Class 1 Felony (victim 60+ or disabled)
elements: Knowingly took property from the person or presence of another
By use of force or by threatening the imminent use of force
enhancements: Class 1 Felony: victim is 60 years of age or older or is a disabled person

offense_class: Class X Felony
elements: Committed a robbery
While carrying on or about person a dangerous weapon
OR while indicating by words or actions possession of a dangerous weapon
enhancements: 15-year mandatory add-on if armed with a firearm
20-year mandatory add-on if firearm discharged
25-year to natural life add-on if firearm discharge caused great bodily harm or death
notes: Mandatory consecutive sentencing enhancements under 720 ILCS 5/33A-2 apply to firearm use.

offense_class: Class 2 Felony; Class X Felony (aggravated)
elements: Knowingly and secretly confined another against their will
OR by force or threat took another from one place to another
enhancements: Aggravated Kidnapping (Class X, 720 ILCS 5/10-2): ransom demand, weapon use, victim under 13, infliction of great bodily harm, victim is police officer

offense_class: Class 2 Felony; Class 1 Felony (residential or occupied structure)
elements: By means of fire or explosive
Knowingly damaged or destroyed any real or personal property
Value over $150 OR which was a dwelling
enhancements: Aggravated Arson (Class X, 720 ILCS 5/20-1.1): person present, fire in place of worship, fire in school
Residential Arson is a Class 1 Felony minimum

offense_class: Class X Felony
elements: Performed a substantial step toward commission of first degree murder
With specific intent to commit first degree murder
enhancements: 10-year mandatory add-on for personal use of a firearm
15-year add-on for discharge of a firearm
20-year add-on for discharge causing great bodily harm or death
notes: Attempt murder is specifically Class X regardless of the general one-class-lower rule. Firearm add-ons are mandatory consecutive.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor to Class 3 Felony
elements: Placed another in reasonable apprehension of receiving a battery
While using a deadly weapon other than a firearm
enhancements: Class 3 Felony if weapon used is a firearm
Further escalation based on victim category

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $500); Class 3 Felony ($500 to $10,000); Class 2 Felony ($10,000 to $100,000)
elements: Knowingly obtained or exerted unauthorized control over another's property
OR obtained by deception, threat, or from lost or mistaken property
With intent to permanently deprive the owner of use and benefit
enhancements: Class 1 Felony: theft over $100,000 from school, place of worship, or government
Class X Felony: theft over $1,000,000

offense_class: Class 3 Felony ($500 to $10,000); Class 2 Felony ($10,000 to $100,000)
elements: Same elements as theft
Property value exceeds $500 threshold
notes: Illinois does not use the term 'grand theft' — all theft is under 720 ILCS 5/16-1 with classification based on value.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $500)
elements: Same elements as theft
Property value under $500
enhancements: Elevates to Class 4 Felony if defendant has a prior theft conviction

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $300); Class 3 Felony ($300+)
elements: Took possession of, carried away, transferred, or caused to be carried away merchandise from a retail establishment
With intent to retain merchandise without paying full retail value
OR altered price tag, transferred merchandise to different container, under-rang register, or returned merchandise not purchased from merchant
enhancements: Organized retail theft (720 ILCS 5/16-30): Class 4 to Class 2 Felony
Prior retail theft conviction elevates classification
notes: Civil recovery statute allows merchants to demand up to $1,000 civilly regardless of criminal prosecution.

offense_class: Class 2 Felony; Class 1 Felony (school, daycare, place of worship)
elements: Without authority
Knowingly entered or remained within a building, structure, or vehicle
With intent to commit therein a felony or theft
enhancements: Residential Burglary (720 ILCS 5/19-3): Class 1 Felony
Home Invasion (720 ILCS 5/19-6): Class X Felony

offense_class: Class 1 Felony
elements: Without authority
Knowingly entered or remained within the dwelling place of another
With intent to commit therein a felony or theft
enhancements: Home Invasion (720 ILCS 5/19-6): Class X Felony if a person is present and defendant is armed
Non-probationable for second offense

offense_class: Class 2 Felony
elements: Without authority entered or remained in a building used for commercial purposes
With intent to commit a felony or theft therein
enhancements: Elevates to Class 1 if committed in school, daycare, or place of worship

offense_class: Class 2 Felony
elements: Knowingly possessed a stolen motor vehicle
OR concealed knowledge that vehicle was stolen
Without owner's consent
enhancements: Class 1 Felony: chop shop operation or VIN alteration (625 ILCS 5/4-103.2)
notes: Unauthorized vehicle taking also charged under 720 ILCS 5/16-1 (theft) or 625 ILCS 5/4-102 (unauthorized use of vehicle).

statute_title: Theft — Obtaining Control Over Stolen Property
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $500); Class 3 to Class 1 Felony (based on value)
elements: Obtained control over stolen property
Knowing the property to be stolen or under circumstances that would reasonably induce belief it was stolen
notes: Illinois does not have a separate receiving stolen property statute — it falls within the general theft statute as subsection (a)(4).

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $500); Class 4 to Class 2 Felony (based on damage amount)
elements: Knowingly damaged the property of another
Without consent of the owner
enhancements: Class 3 Felony: damage $500 to $10,000 or damage to school, church, or fire department
Class 2 Felony: damage $10,000 to $100,000
Class 1 Felony: damage over $100,000

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor; Class A Misdemeanor (residences, schools, farmland)
elements: Entered or remained on or in property of another
After receiving notice from the owner that entry was forbidden
OR remained after being directed to leave by owner or authorized person
enhancements: Criminal Trespass to a Residence (720 ILCS 5/19-4): Class A Misdemeanor

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor to Class 1 Felony
elements: Knowingly damaged or destroyed the property of another
OR knowingly started a fire on another's land without consent
notes: Illinois calls this 'Criminal Damage to Property' — same statute (720 ILCS 5/21-1) as vandalism.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (1st offense); Class 4 Felony (2nd+ or against pregnant victim)
elements: Intentionally or knowingly caused bodily harm
OR made physical contact of insulting or provoking nature
With a family or household member
enhancements: Class 4 Felony: second or subsequent offense or committed against pregnant victim
Class 3 Felony: third+ offense
Aggravated Domestic Battery (720 ILCS 5/12-3.3): Class 2 Felony for strangulation or great bodily harm
notes: Illinois Domestic Violence Act (750 ILCS 60) provides civil remedies. Mandatory no-contact order on arrest.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (1st); Class 4 Felony (2nd+)
elements: Intentionally or knowingly caused bodily harm to family or household member
OR made physical contact of insulting or provoking nature with family or household member
enhancements: Aggravated Domestic Battery (720 ILCS 5/12-3.3): Class 2 Felony for strangulation or great bodily harm
notes: Conviction requires completion of a domestic battery counseling program.

statute_title: Endangering the Life or Health of a Child
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Class 3 Felony if great bodily harm results
elements: Willfully caused or permitted a child under 18
To be placed in circumstances that endangered the child's life or health
enhancements: Class 3 Felony: great bodily harm or permanent disability results
Class 2 Felony: death of child results

offense_class: Class X Felony
elements: Intentionally or knowingly caused great bodily harm, permanent disability, or disfigurement
To a child under 13 years of age
enhancements: Natural life if child dies as a result
notes: Illinois DCFS administrative proceedings run parallel to criminal prosecution.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (1st); Class 4 Felony (2nd+ or stalking violation)
elements: Order of protection was in effect
Defendant had actual knowledge of the order
Committed an act in violation of the order's specific terms
enhancements: Class 4 Felony: second+ violation or violation involving stalking or surveillance
Class 3 Felony: second+ violation involving domestic battery
notes: Order of protection issued under the Illinois Domestic Violence Act (750 ILCS 60) or Civil No Contact Order Act.

offense_class: Class 4 Felony (1st); Class 3 Felony (2nd+)
elements: On at least 2 separate occasions
Followed, monitored, observed, surveilled, threatened, or communicated to or about a specific person
Knowing that conduct would cause a reasonable person to fear for their safety
Actually caused the victim to fear for their safety
enhancements: Aggravated Stalking (720 ILCS 5/12-7.4): Class 3 Felony — violates court order, uses weapon, victim under 18
Class 1 Felony for certain aggravated circumstances

statute_title: Harassment by Telephone or Electronic Communication
offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (1st); Class A Misdemeanor (2nd+)
elements: Made a telephone call or electronic communication
With intent to harass, threaten, or intimidate another person
Content was obscene, threatening, or defendant repeatedly contacted to annoy
enhancements: Class 4 Felony if made to a minor under 18 or violates an order of protection

statute_title: Criminal Abuse or Neglect of an Elderly or Disabled Person
offense_class: Class 3 Felony; Class 2 Felony (great bodily harm)
elements: Had a duty of care for a person 60 years of age or older or a disabled adult
Knowingly or intentionally abused, neglected, or financially exploited that person
enhancements: Class 2 Felony: great bodily harm results
Class 1 Felony: death results
notes: Also prosecuted under the Adult Protective Services Act (320 ILCS 20). Financial exploitation is a separate offense under 720 ILCS 5/17-56.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor to Class 4 Felony depending on circumstances
elements: Sold, manufactured, transferred, purchased, possessed, or carried a weapon
In circumstances prohibited by law (concealed without license, in vehicle without proper storage, switchblade, tear gas, etc.)
enhancements: Aggravated UUW (720 ILCS 5/24-1.6): Class 4 to Class 1 Felony for prior felony or possessing while masked
notes: Illinois requires a FOID card for all firearm possession. Carrying without FOID or CCLC triggers UUW.

statute_title: Unlawful Use or Possession of Weapons by Felon
offense_class: Class 3 Felony; Class 2 Felony (second+ offense)
elements: Convicted of a felony or adjudicated delinquent for a felony offense
Possessed any firearm, firearm ammunition, or Taser
OR possessed explosive bullets
enhancements: Class 2 Felony: second+ offense or possession of assault weapon
notes: Non-probationable: Illinois law bars probation for convicted felons possessing firearms.

statute_title: Unlawful Use of Weapons — Concealed Carry Violation
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor to Class 4 Felony
elements: Carried a concealed firearm
Without a valid Illinois Concealed Carry License
OR carried in a statutorily prohibited location (school, government building, bar, etc.)
enhancements: Aggravated UUW for prohibited locations: Class 4 Felony
Carrying while FOID revoked: Class 3 Felony
notes: Illinois CCLC required in addition to FOID card.

offense_class: Class 4 Felony
elements: Recklessly discharged a firearm
In a manner that endangered the bodily safety of another person
enhancements: Aggravated Discharge of Firearm (720 ILCS 5/24-1.2): Class 1 Felony — discharge in direction of person, occupied vehicle, school, or law enforcement

statute_title: Unlawful Sale or Delivery of Firearms
offense_class: Class 4 Felony; Class 2 Felony (aggravated)
elements: Knowingly sold or transferred a firearm
To a person prohibited from possessing firearms (felon, minor, intoxicated person, etc.)
OR sold without routing through an FFL dealer for a background check
enhancements: Aggravated: sale of assault weapon or sale to known gang member

statute_title: Unlawful Use of Weapons — Prohibited Weapons
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor to Class 4 Felony
elements: Possessed a weapon prohibited under Illinois law
Including switchblades, brass knuckles, metal-piercing bullets, stun guns without FOID, illegal silencers, or machine guns
notes: Assault weapons ban enacted in 2023 (PA 102-1116) is subject to ongoing litigation as of 2026.

statute_title: Aggravated Unlawful Use of a Weapon
offense_class: Class 4 Felony (1st); Class 1 Felony (2nd+ or prior firearm conviction)
elements: Carried or possessed a loaded firearm on person or accessible in a vehicle
Was not on own land or in own dwelling
AND: did not have FOID card; weapon was uncased; had prior felony; or was under 21 without parental permission
enhancements: Class 1 Felony: second+ conviction under this section
notes: AUUW is among the most commonly charged gun offenses in Illinois. Non-probationable for first-time felony offenders.

offense_class: Class 4 Felony
elements: Used a computer, telecommunications device, or electronic medium
To commit fraud or deceit
For the purpose of financial gain
notes: Federal wire fraud (18 U.S.C. 1343) is often charged instead in multi-state schemes. Illinois state charge used for intrastate fraud.

offense_class: Class 4 Felony (under $300); Class 3 to Class 1 Felony (based on loss amount)
elements: Knowingly used another person's personal identifying information
With intent to fraudulently obtain credit, money, goods, services, or other property
OR to commit any other crime
enhancements: Class 3 Felony: loss $300 to $2,000
Class 2 Felony: loss $2,000 to $10,000
Class 1 Felony: loss over $10,000 or victim is 60+

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $500); Class 3 to Class 1 Felony (based on value)
elements: Obtained lawful possession of property
Converted that property to personal use without authorization
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Illinois does not have a separate embezzlement statute. Covered under general theft statute 720 ILCS 5/16-1 as 'theft by lawful possession'.

offense_class: Class 3 Felony; Class 2 Felony (financial instrument)
elements: With intent to defraud
Made, altered, delivered, endorsed, or possessed any writing appearing to be genuine when it was not
Writing created, modified, or terminated legal rights, obligations, or status
enhancements: Class 2 Felony: forgery of check, bond, deed, will, or other financial instrument

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $150); Class 4 to Class 1 Felony (based on amount)
elements: Knowingly issued or delivered a check or draft
With intent to defraud
Knowing at time of delivery there were insufficient funds on deposit
enhancements: Class 4 Felony: amount $150 to $1,000
Class 3 Felony: amount $1,000 to $10,000
Class 1 Felony: amount over $100,000

offense_class: Class 4 Felony (under $300); Class 3 to Class 1 Felony (based on amount)
elements: Knowingly obtained or attempted to obtain insurance benefits through material misrepresentation
OR knowingly submitted a false or fraudulent insurance claim

statute_title: Fraudulent Use of Electronic Transmission — Credit Card Fraud
offense_class: Class 4 Felony
elements: Used another person's credit card, debit card, or account number
Without authorization
To obtain money, goods, or services
enhancements: Class 3 Felony: amount over $300 in a 6-month period

offense_class: Class 3 Felony (under $10,000); Class 1 Felony (over $100,000)
fine_max: Twice the amount laundered or $500,000, whichever is greater
elements: Conducted or attempted to conduct a financial transaction
Knowing proceeds were derived from criminal activity
With intent to promote criminal activity OR conceal nature or source of proceeds

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $300); Class 4 to Class 1 Felony (based on amount)
elements: By means of false pretense, false statement, or fraudulent misrepresentation
Obtained money, property, services, or other thing of value
Or caused another to execute a document affecting property

statute_title: Deceptive Practices — Bank or Financial Institution Fraud
offense_class: Class 1 Felony (large amounts)
elements: Knowingly executed or attempted to execute a scheme to defraud a financial institution
By means of false or fraudulent pretenses, representations, or promises
To obtain money, funds, or other property under the custody of a financial institution
notes: Bank fraud is typically prosecuted federally under 18 U.S.C. 1344. Illinois state prosecution uses deceptive practices statute.

offense_class: Class 1 Felony; Class X Felony (aggravated)
elements: Committed an act of sexual penetration
By use of force or threat of force
OR knew victim was unable to give knowing consent
OR was related to victim under 18, was a family member, or held a position of trust or authority over the victim
enhancements: Aggravated Criminal Sexual Assault (720 ILCS 5/11-1.30): Class X — weapon displayed, great bodily harm inflicted, victim under 9, perpetrator over 17 and victim under 13
notes: Truth-in-sentencing: must serve 85% of sentence. SORA registration required.

offense_class: Class 1 Felony; Class X Felony (aggravated)
elements: Committed an act of sexual penetration
By use of force or threat of force
Without consent of victim
enhancements: Predatory Criminal Sexual Assault (720 ILCS 5/11-1.40): Class X — penetration of victim under 13 by perpetrator 17 or older; mandatory 6 to 60 years
notes: Illinois eliminated the term 'rape' in 1984. The offense is Criminal Sexual Assault under 720 ILCS 5/11-1.20.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Class 4 Felony (3rd+ offense)
elements: In a public place
Performed a sexual act or exposed body parts
In a lewd manner in the presence of another person
enhancements: Class 4 Felony for third+ conviction
SORA registration may be required if victim is under 17

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (1st); Class 4 Felony (2nd+)
elements: Offered or agreed to perform a sexual act for any money or thing of value
OR solicited another person to perform a sexual act for compensation
enhancements: Class 4 Felony: solicitation within 1,000 feet of school or place of worship
Class 3 Felony: solicitation of person under 18

statute_title: Traveling to Meet a Minor / Grooming
offense_class: Class 3 Felony (grooming); Class 2 Felony (traveling to meet)
elements: Used electronic communication to solicit a minor
For purpose of engaging in sexual activity
OR traveled to meet a minor for sexual purposes after online solicitation
enhancements: Class 2 Felony if defendant traveled to meet minor
SORA registration required

offense_class: Class 1 Felony (possession); Class X Felony (production or distribution)
elements: Photographed, filmed, videotaped, created, or possessed a depiction of a child under 18
Engaged in sexual conduct or depicted in a lewd manner
OR disseminated such material
enhancements: Each image or video counts as a separate offense
Mandatory SORA registration for life
Mandatory consecutive sentences for multiple counts
notes: Non-probationable. Lifetime sex offender registration required.

statute_title: Failure to Register as a Sex Offender
offense_class: Class 3 Felony (1st); Class 2 Felony (2nd+)
elements: Required to register as a sex offender under the Illinois Sex Offender Registration Act
Knowingly failed to register or verify address within 3 days of establishing residence
enhancements: Class 2 Felony for second or subsequent failure to register
notes: Registration required within 3 days of establishing residence. Annual or quarterly updates required depending on offense classification.

offense_class: Class 4 Felony; Class A Misdemeanor (certain age combinations)
elements: Committed an act of sexual conduct or sexual penetration
With a person between 13 and 17 years of age
Defendant was at least 5 years older than the victim
enhancements: Aggravated Criminal Sexual Abuse (720 ILCS 5/11-1.60): Class 2 Felony — victim under 13, defendant in position of trust or authority, defendant is family member
notes: Consensual sex between a 13 to 16 year old and someone less than 5 years older is not criminal in Illinois.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor to Class 2 Felony
elements: Committed an act of sexual conduct (touching)
By force or threat of force
OR with a person incapable of giving knowing consent
enhancements: Aggravated Criminal Sexual Abuse (720 ILCS 5/11-1.60): Class 2 Felony
notes: Sexual conduct (touching) vs. sexual penetration determines criminal sexual abuse vs. criminal sexual assault.

statute_title: Criminal Sexual Abuse (equivalent to sexual battery)
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor to Class 2 Felony
elements: Committed an act of sexual conduct by force or threat
OR with a victim unable to give knowing consent
notes: Illinois does not use the term 'sexual battery.' Criminal Sexual Abuse (720 ILCS 5/11-1.50) covers equivalent conduct.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor (most acts); Class 4 Felony (false fire or emergency report)
elements: Knowingly did any act in a manner that is unreasonably annoying, alarming, or dangerous
Which provoked a breach of the peace
enhancements: Class A Misdemeanor: peeping tom, transmitting false police report
Class 4 Felony: false 911 report or false report of fire, bomb, or disaster

statute_title: Resisting or Obstructing a Peace Officer
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Class 4 Felony (injury to officer)
elements: Knowingly resisted or obstructed the performance of
Any authorized act within the official capacity
Of a peace officer, correctional officer, or firefighter
enhancements: Class 4 Felony: officer suffers injury during the resistance

offense_class: Class 4 Felony
elements: Knowingly destroyed, altered, concealed, or disguised physical evidence
OR planted false evidence
OR furnished false information
With intent to prevent apprehension or obstruct prosecution of any person for any crime
enhancements: Class 3 Felony if obstruction relates to a Class 1, 2, or X felony case

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (direct); Class 4 Felony (indirect or continuing)
elements: Knowingly failed to comply with a court order or perform a court-ordered duty
OR disrupted court proceedings
OR willfully disobeyed a lawful process or order of court
notes: Courts retain inherent contempt power for immediate sanctions up to 6 months without a formal charge.

statute_title: Loitering for Drug or Sexual Purposes
offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (basic); Class A Misdemeanor (drug or sex purpose loitering)
elements: Remained in a public place with intent to engage in drug activity or solicit a sexual act
OR remained in a place without lawful purpose after being asked to leave by an officer
notes: Basic loitering ordinances are typically municipal. State loitering statutes focus on drug or sex-purpose loitering.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor
elements: Knowingly engaged in fighting, threatening, or violent behavior
OR created unreasonable noise or disturbance
That provoked a breach of the peace
notes: Illinois consolidates disturbing the peace under the disorderly conduct statute.

offense_class: Class 4 Felony (felony underlying case); Class A Misdemeanor (misdemeanor case)
elements: Released on bail or personal recognizance
Knowingly failed to appear before the court as required by conditions of release
With intent to avoid prosecution
notes: Under the SAFE-T Act (2021), Illinois moved to a no-cash-bail system. Failure to appear remains a criminal offense.

statute_title: Disorderly Conduct — False Report of Emergency
offense_class: Class 4 Felony
elements: Transmitted a false report
That a fire, explosion, crime, catastrophe, or other emergency was occurring
To any law enforcement agency, fire department, or emergency management agency
enhancements: Felony counts for each separate false report transmitted

offense_class: Class 3 Felony; Class 2 Felony (aggravated)
elements: Communicated to another a threat to perform an action prohibited by law
With intent to cause that person to perform or omit an act against their will
OR with intent to cause fear in that person
enhancements: Aggravated Intimidation (720 ILCS 5/12-6.1): Class 2 Felony if against public officials or crime victims
Threatening a Public Official (720 ILCS 5/12-9): Class 4 Felony

statute_title: Violation of Probation or Conditional Discharge
offense_class: Dependent on underlying offense class
elements: Was serving a term of probation or conditional discharge
Violated one or more conditions of probation
Violation proven by preponderance of the evidence
enhancements: New criminal offense during probation: presumption against continued probation
Court may impose original sentence or modify conditions
notes: Violations heard by the sentencing judge. Standard of proof is preponderance. Defendant may be held without bail pending hearing.

offense_class: Administrative — depends on underlying offense
elements: Failed to report to probation officer as required
Failed drug or alcohol test
Failed to complete required community service hours
Failed to pay fines or restitution
OR other non-criminal condition violation
notes: Under the SAFE-T Act, court must consider less restrictive alternatives before revoking probation for technical violations.

statute_title: Substantive Violation of Probation — New Criminal Offense
offense_class: Underlying offense class
elements: Committed a new criminal offense while on probation
New offense proven by preponderance or separate criminal conviction
enhancements: May result in revocation and imposition of original sentence plus new sentence running consecutively

offense_class: Administrative revocation proceeding
penalty_max: Return to IDOC for balance of sentence
elements: Was on mandatory supervised release (MSR)
Violated one or more conditions of MSR
Violation proven by preponderance at Prisoner Review Board hearing
notes: In Illinois, parole is called Mandatory Supervised Release (MSR). Violations heard by Prisoner Review Board, not courts.

offense_class: Administrative — Prisoner Review Board proceeding
penalty_max: Return to IDOC for remainder of sentence
elements: Released on MSR following IDOC sentence
Violated conditions of release (new offense, failed drug test, absconded, etc.)
notes: Illinois uses 'Mandatory Supervised Release' rather than 'parole.' Revocation is administrative through the Prisoner Review Board.

offense_class: One class below the most serious offense that is the object of the conspiracy
penalty_max: One class below target offense maximum
elements: With intent that an offense be committed
Agreed with one or more other persons to commit or attempt to commit an offense
AND any one of them performed an overt act in furtherance of the agreement
enhancements: Conspiracy to commit a Class X Felony is a Class 1 Felony
No overt act required for Class X conspiracy if target is drug trafficking

statute_title: Use of Force in Defense of Person — Affirmative Defense
offense_class: Affirmative defense — not a criminal charge
elements: Defendant reasonably believed use of force was necessary
To defend against another's imminent use of unlawful force
Force used was not greater than reasonably necessary to prevent the harm
notes: Illinois self-defense is an affirmative defense. Defendant must produce some evidence; state must disprove beyond reasonable doubt. Castle Doctrine codified at 720 ILCS 5/7-2.

offense_class: Varies
notes: Placeholder for Illinois charges not covered by specific taxonomy entries. Consult 720 ILCS 5 (Criminal Code of 2012) and other Illinois compiled statutes.
